q: The Cape's founding vintage year under Jan van Riebeeck was:
exp: 'Today, praise be to God, wine was pressed for the first time from Cape grapes' — 2 Feb 1659.

q: Which 1925 crossing created Pinotage, and at which university?
ans: Prof. Abraham Perold at Stellenbosch: Pinot Noir × Cinsaut ('Hermitage')
exp: The seedlings survived in a garden after Perold forgot them — rescued by a passing lecturer.

q: The Swartland Revolution's manifesto wines, Columella and Palladius, come from which producer?
exp: Old-vine Rhône reds and Mediterranean whites off schist and granite; the Ouwingerdreeks series maps heritage vineyards.

q: What does the Certified Heritage Vineyards seal (Old Vine Project) require?
ans: Documented vines 35+ years old, with the planting date on the seal

q: Hemel-en-Aarde's three appellations ascend from the sea as:
ans: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley → Upper Hemel-en-Aarde → Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge
exp: Clay-rich shales; Hamilton Russell, Storm and Crystallum parse the wards.

q: Which Stellenbosch estate's 'Paul Sauer' is the Cape's classic Bordeaux blend?
exp: Also the standard-bearer for serious Pinotage (Black Label from 1953 vines).

q: Vin de Constance is revived at which estate?
exp: Unfortified sun-raisined Muscat de Frontignan; Napoleon's St Helena consolation.

q: The False Bay breeze cooling Stellenbosch afternoons is locally the:
exp: It scrubs disease and drops summer temperatures by degrees.

exp: Mullineux bottles the same variety off three soils — a masterclass in terroir argument.

q: South Africa's Wine of Origin scheme dates from which year?
exp: 1973: WO wards, districts, regions; 100% origin for the stated area.

q: 'Steen' historically named which grape in the Cape?
exp: South Africa grows more Chenin than all of France.

q: South Africa's Wine of Origin scheme sets minimum percentages for the three claims on a label. Which set is correct?
exp: Origin is absolute — every grape in a WO wine must come from the stated ward, district, region or geographical unit, with no tolerance at all. Vintage and cultivar each carry an 85% minimum, which is also the threshold the EU accepts for export. The takeaway: in South Africa the appellation claim is the strict one, unlike the varietal and vintage claims, which behave like most New World law.

q: What must a block satisfy to be certified 'Single Vineyard' under the Wine of Origin scheme?
accept: registered block no larger than 6 hectares planted to a single variety
maximum six hectares one cultivar registered with wo
single cultivar under 6 ha registered vineyard unit
ans: It must be registered with the WO authority, be no larger than 6 hectares, and be planted to a single variety, farmed as one unit
exp: South Africa legislated site specificity long before most of the New World: the Single Vineyard designation exists precisely so a producer can name a block on the label. The 6 ha ceiling is what keeps it meaningful — it prevents 'single vineyard' being stretched over a whole farm. Note the difference from 'Estate Wine', which concerns ownership and contiguous property with cellar and bottling on site, not size.

q: Which Wine of Origin district was created in 2017 to gather the wards of Constantia, Durbanville, Hout Bay and Philadelphia?
ans: Cape Town (a district of the Coastal Region)
exp: Before 2017 Constantia and Durbanville were free-floating wards inside the Coastal Region with no district above them. Grouping them as the Cape Town district gave the city's cool, maritime, largely Sauvignon-and-Semillon vineyards a single marketable name and tidied the four-tier hierarchy (geographical unit, region, district, ward). Candidates who learned the map a decade ago routinely miss it.

q: Under the EU trade agreement South Africa surrendered the word 'port' on its labels. What replaced it for the Calitzdorp style?
opts: Karoo Vintage, Karoo Ruby, Karoo Tawny, Karoo Reserve
Cape Vintage, Cape Ruby, Cape Tawny, Cape LBV
Muscadel Rood, Muscadel Wit, Jerepigo, Hanepoot
Cape Fortified Red, with sweetness stated in grams
exp: The 'Cape' prefix carries the whole family: Cape Ruby, Cape Tawny, Cape Vintage, Cape Vintage Reserve and Cape Late Bottled Vintage, made largely in Calitzdorp (a district of the Klein Karoo) from Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca and Souzão. Muscadel and jerepigo are the other Cape fortified tradition — muscat-based and mistelle-styled — so option three is a real category, just the wrong one.

q: Name the ward that is South Africa's southernmost vineyard area, lying in the Cape Agulhas district and known for taut Sauvignon Blanc and peppery Syrah.
exp: Elim sits within sight of Africa's southern tip, raked by wind off two oceans, and its Sauvignon is the Cape's most overtly saline and green-fig style. Learn the nesting: Elim (ward) inside Cape Agulhas (district) inside Cape South Coast (region) — the same region that holds Walker Bay, Elgin and Overberg.
